newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks recover in livelier trade.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks recover in livelier trade.

text.p: Croatian stocks recovered on Wednesday in lively trade but analysts said hoteliers shares were expected to stabilise at lower prices amid weaker demand.
"Despite somewhat higher closing prices of most hoteliers' issues in today's trading, an imminent correction is likely," Zoran Ilic of Consult Invest brokerage said.
He said the number of buying orders compared with the selling ones is running low and the prices of hotel stocks are likely to go down by the end of the week.
"Lower liquidity is a signal that the prices would go down," Ilic added.
Arenaturist gained 20 kuna to close at 180, Istraturist was up 4 kuna to 209 and Jadranturist remained flat at 325 kuna, but on meagre volumes of a few hundred shares each.
The only very active hotelier, Suncani Hvar, lost one kuna to close at 64 on volume of 2,235 shares.

Ilic said he expected other stocks, especially blue chips Pliva, Zagrebacka Banka, and food stocks Kras and Podravka, which were most actively traded on Wednesday, to stabilise around the current level or higher.
Leading commercial bank Zagrebacka closed at 1,890 kuna, 30 up from Tuesday, after trading in the 1,850-1,865 kuna range for most of the day on volume of 3,024 shares.
Drugs firm Pliva edged down five kuna to 485, with 1,070 shares sold.
Chocolate maker Kras gained 10 to close at 490 on 2,129 shares and Ilic said it was a realistic price that is likely to hold in the short-term run.
Podravka firmed 1.9 kuna to 319.9 on volume of 2,953 units.
Top gainer was liquor factory Badel, which added 41.25 kuna to 130, selling 145 units in a first deal this year.
A 200-share package in brewery Karlovacka Pivovara was sold at 235 kuna each, 21 up from when they last traded in 1996.
Biggest decliner Adriatic oil pipeline operator Janaf lost 800 kuna to 6,200, with only one share traded.
Nine of 15 active stocks rose, four were down and two were flat. Volume was slightly higher at 13,851 shares, turnover was 9.4 million kuna, up from 7.1.
